subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): import legacy auth-profiles.json into SQLite store on load

question: Should legacy `auth-profiles.json` be imported during normal auth runtime loads, or must recovery stay in doctor/startup migration before runtime reads?
rationale: The bug and proof are credible, but the proposed fix crosses a credential-bearing migration boundary where current policy, docs, and tests keep legacy JSON out of steady-state runtime loads.

options.title: Keep Runtime SQLite-Only
options.body: Rework recovery into doctor or an explicit startup/update migration that verifies SQLite persistence and handles legacy JSON cleanup under migration rules.

options.title: Approve Runtime Import
options.body: Accept runtime import only with maintainer/security approval plus updated invariant tests, docs, and a clear stale-credential threat model.

options.title: Pause For Canonical Issue
options.body: Pause this branch while the broader migration and fallback diagnostics are handled through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100067.

recommendation.title: Keep Runtime SQLite-Only
recommendation.body: Rework recovery into doctor or an explicit startup/update migration that verifies SQLite persistence and handles legacy JSON cleanup under migration rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the auth persistence runtime boundary introduced and repeatedly maintained in recent auth-profile history.
